eyebrow: Eat Like a Local in Yala · Updated 2026
intro: Yala is a city that eats well without making a fuss about it. Huge pots of guay jab in front of old hotels, grilled fish seafood near the railway station, all the way up to Cantonese food and early morning dim sum in Betong — all in one province. We picked 10 restaurants that Yala locals actually eat at and that out-of-towners have never left disappointed.

blocks.html:
If you were to tell Yala's story through food, it's a city with two distinct rhythms inside one province. In the city of Yala you'll find a beautiful roundabout-grid layout, an old market where the smell of ancient coffee drifts out from early morning, guay jab with fragrant Chinese-spice pork broth that people queue for before sunrise, and hot beef soup down a lane in front of the railway station that has been open for decades. Drive south up into the mountains to Betong and the atmosphere shifts into a Chinese hill town — Cantonese food, crispy-skin Betong chicken, and early-morning dim sum are the daily rhythm of the people there. Yala is where Chinese food, Southern Thai food, and Halal food live comfortably side by side, and you can eat across the whole spectrum without ever repeating a flavour.

Several restaurants in this list are genuine legends. Guay Jab Wing Gai Thep Wiman (Hia Tong) has been a fixture of Yala for over 70 years. Thara Seafood carries the "Good Stuff of Yala City" badge from the provincial chamber of commerce. Tai See Hee dim sum in Betong has been going for around 80 years. Ta Yern (Kitti), Betong's oldest Chinese restaurant, is a stop on every trip. And Charoen Khao Man Gai Betong Panthu Tae (Sor Tor Maew) uses 100% genuine Betong chicken with its naturally springy skin. We've ordered the list from small bites in the city through to a full Chinese banquet table in Betong — if you're planning a trip to the southern border provinces, keep this list close and work through it one restaurant at a time.

blocks.name: Guay Jab Wing Gai Thep Wiman (Hia Tong)
blocks.signature: Guay jab with chicken wings, rich palo spice broth, thick-cut crispy pork
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Yala and want a morning meal the way locals have been eating it for generations, Guay Jab Wing Gai Thep Wiman — which everyone simply calls "Hia Tong" — is the name locals give you first. The restaurant has been part of the city for over 70 years, passed down from the original generation to Hia Tong (Worawit), who still runs the soup pot every morning. The signature is a Chinese-style guay jab with chicken wings, braised drumsticks, and leg meat slow-cooked until falling-off-the-bone tender. The broth is a deep palo with Chinese medicinal herbs: complex, rounded, not cloying — a flavour hard to find in ordinary guay jab shops.

The must-order is guay jab with chicken wings and palo egg: wings and drumsticks braised until the meat slides off, clean offal with no smell, firm bounce, and palo eggs beautifully coloured through with the broth. For those who want more chew, thick-cut crispy pork is available as an add-on. Customers consistently say "the broth is intense and fragrant with spices," "the chicken is perfectly braised," and that nothing else tastes quite as good as this one. The guay jab noodles come out perfectly soft. Order a Chinese doughnut on the side to dip in the broth — the classic way to eat it here.

The restaurant is a double shophouse on the corner of Si Bamrung Road, next to Thep Wiman Hotel, across from Yala Rama Hotel, in the old-town neighbourhood near the market. Classic old Chinese street food atmosphere, clean and comfortable. Opens early from around 6:30am to noon. Under 100 THB per bowl, starting at just over 50 THB — excellent value for something that has been simmering overnight.

The key thing to know: the restaurant only operates mornings until noon, and closes when they sell out. Late risers may miss it. Come early to get the full menu with no wait — the best way to start your first day in Yala.
mustOrder: Guay jab with chicken wing and palo egg
blocks.bestFor: First breakfast in Yala / old-town must-try
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: street food · Charles Haynes / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Ta Yern (Kitti) Betong
blocks.signature: Chopped Betong chicken, steamed fish with plum, Khao Yok — braised pork belly with taro
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Betong local where to eat and "Ta Yern (Kitti)" comes up first almost every time. This is a nearly 40-year-old Chinese restaurant that Pa Lek — Khun Kitti Yongwiriyakul — built from a wooden shophouse into a busy two-storey building on Sukyang Road, next to Betong Plaza and near the clock tower. Easy to walk to from the town centre. The best option for first-time Betong visitors who want the famous dishes without any guesswork, or for families and groups because the portions are large and the menu is long.

Every table orders the "chopped Betong chicken": firm yet tender meat, naturally crispy skin, dressed with the restaurant's own soy sauce and fried garlic — the real star, because Ta Yern runs its own traditional soy-sauce fermentation house. Reviewers consistently say the sauce is what transforms an ordinary chicken dish into something unforgettable. Follow that with "steamed fish with plum" — sweet, clean farm-raised fish steamed with pickled plum and ginger, sour-salty and beautifully balanced — and "Khao Yok": Hakka-style pork belly braised with taro until both melt on the tongue. A genuine Betong Chinese classic.

Two floors: ground floor is no-AC with close-together tables; upstairs has air conditioning and fits large groups comfortably. Per-head cost around 251–500 THB. The Betong chicken dishes run to 500 THB for a large plate — some reviews note the chicken price feels steep, but most conclude the portion and flavour justify it. Food comes out quickly, service is efficient.

A heads-up: evenings get very crowded and you should expect a wait. The roast pork and steamed bun dishes usually sell out within a few hours of morning opening — call ahead to reserve those. For sour, try the mango salad. For vegetables, ask for pak nam stir-fried with garlic oil, a local Betong green. Guaranteed original Betong Chinese food for every visit.
mustOrder: Chopped Betong chicken with fried-garlic soy sauce
Khao Yok — braised pork belly with taro
Pak nam stir-fried with garlic oil
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Betong / families and groups

blocks.name: Thara Seafood
blocks.signature: Herb-grilled fish, crab fried rice, restaurant's house seafood dipping sauce
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Yala local which seafood restaurant to take out-of-town guests to and "Thara Seafood" is almost always the first answer. The restaurant has been a Yala institution for over thirty years, on Phiphat Road in the old-town neighbourhood near Yala Railway Station. A classic, unfussy old shophouse with no pretension, but with the kind of flavour that locals have been loyal to for generations. Good for families or groups who want quality traditional seafood cooking and the lived-in character of a place that has been passed down through the generations.

Every table must have the herb-grilled fish: a sea bass or threadfin wrapped in a paste of blended pandan and basil, folded in banana leaf, and grilled over charcoal until fragrant. The fish is tender, the herb note is unmistakable. Reviewers consistently call it "the best grilled fish I've ever had." The crab fried rice gets real crab meat, and the house seafood dipping sauce — the quiet standout — has a clean, layered heat that many diners say makes it a signature of the restaurant on its own. Garlic-pepper prawns, seafood tom yum, glass noodle salad, and mussels stir-fried with roasted chilli paste all round out the table well.

Pricing around 251–500 THB per person — reasonable for fresh seafood changed daily. The restaurant's sustained popularity shows in its consistent review scores and the "Good Stuff of Yala City" badge from the provincial chamber of commerce. Central location near the railway station makes it easy to drop in for both lunch and dinner. Open daily 11:00–21:00.

Good to know: on holiday evenings tables fill fast. If you're coming in a group or want a particularly fine grilled fish, calling ahead is worth it. Grilled fish is done individually to order, so allow a little extra time for it to come out.
mustOrder: Mussels stir-fried with roasted chilli paste
blocks.bestFor: Evening seafood dinner with family or friends in Yala city
blocks.spice: Both spicy and non-spicy options, adjustable

blocks.name: Charoen Khao Man Gai Betong Panthu Tae (Sor Tor Maew)
blocks.signature: Genuine Betong chicken rice — springy crispy skin, firm tender meat, fragrant rice
blocks.descHtml:
Ask anyone in Betong which chicken rice stall is the best and "Charoen Khao Man Gai Betong Panthu Tae — Sor Tor Maew" floats to the top every time. The restaurant has been in Betong for over 30 years, selling chicken rice made exclusively from 100% genuine Betong chicken — a native Chinese-heritage breed raised locally for so long it has become the district's calling card. Perfect for anyone who just arrived in Betong and wants a first meal that justifies the journey, or for dedicated food-seekers tracking down the authentic original.

The must-order is Betong chicken rice: chopped chicken with firm-yet-tender meat and naturally springy, crispy skin — characteristic of genuine Betong chicken, low in fat, lightly dressed with seasoned dark soy sauce. Served with fragrant, well-cooked rice, a clear bone broth, and two dipping sauce styles. If plain chicken isn't enough, there's also roast pork rice, red pork rice, pork trotter rice, and fried chicken rice to choose from. Most reviewers praise the neatly chewy but non-mushy meat, the crispy skin, and the authenticity of a genuine Betong chicken that's hard to find anywhere else.

Straightforward, honest restaurant atmosphere — emphasis on flavour over décor. Busy on holidays with both Thai and Malaysian-Singaporean tourists. Prices are gentle, well under 100 THB per plate. Location: 202 Sukyang Road, central Betong, near the clock tower roundabout, across from the old TOT telephone exchange — easy to find. Open daily 06:00–14:00.

Important to note: the restaurant closes at 2pm and genuine Betong chicken is limited in supply. On holiday mornings items may sell out fast. To get a full selection of parts, come early. Some reviews mention that during peak hours the queue can feel a bit chaotic — allow a little extra time. Once you taste real Betong chicken, you'll understand completely why this is a landmark stop that no one skips.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Betong / chasing the authentic original

blocks.name: Tai See Hee (Tai See Hee)
blocks.signature: Morning dim sum, red pork bao, Ji Chong Fan
blocks.descHtml:
Tai See Hee — "Ta Si Si" meaning four-direction prosperity — is the early morning dim sum house that has been in Betong for decades, now in its third generation. Positioned right at the junction near Betong Mongkhon Rit Tunnel. For anyone visiting Betong who wants to start the day exactly the way locals do, this is the landmark everyone pins. It suits dim sum lovers who like the atmosphere of an old Chinese teahouse where sharing a table with strangers feels completely natural.

The most talked-about item is "Ji Chong Fan" — thick fresh rice noodles hand-cut from rice-flour dough, dressed with soy sauce, sprinkled with sesame and fried garlic, served alongside braised pork ribs in black bean sauce — a salty, sweetly rounded combination. Follow with red pork steamed bao (soft dough, packed filling), steaming dim sum baskets rolling continuously from the kitchen, and taro fritters that multiple reviews have given more than full marks to. The restaurant makes everything in-house with over 30 varieties. Finish with a pot of fragrant hot Chinese tea that pairs perfectly with the dim sum. Reviewers almost unanimously say: delicious, fresh, constantly replenished.

Very reasonable price — many people get through a meal here for around 120 THB. Come in a group and go all out and you're still in the low hundreds per head. Atmosphere is lively from before sunrise — Betong locals, Thai tourists, and Malaysian visitors all mixed together. Two floors: when the ground floor fills, staff guide you upstairs. Opens from around 5am until about 11am. Google scores 4.3 from hundreds of reviews, which explains why it's packed every single morning.

The key thing to know: this place fills up fast — try to arrive before 6:30am, because after that tables go and you'll be waiting in line. Parking in the area is tight because it's central Betong. If you're staying in town, walking is easier. Since it's an all-morning restaurant, coming late may mean missing certain items that sell out fast. Come early, get the full experience of a proper old Chinese teahouse.
blocks.bestFor: Betong morning dim sum the local way

Base yourself in Yala city to walk the old-town breakfast spots and the market. Betong deserves its own overnight stay so you can catch morning dim sum and drive up to see the Aiyoeweng sea of mist. A central location is best for getting to restaurants on foot. Compare Yala–Betong hotel prices and reviews before locking your dates.

blocks.name: Annur Khao Mok Arabic (ANNUR Restaurant)
blocks.area: 4/1 Mueang Mai Market, Sateng Subdistrict, Mueang Yala District, Yala Province
blocks.signature: Goat biryani rice — fragrant spiced rice with tender meat
blocks.descHtml:
To understand the appeal of Arabic Halal food in Yala city, ANNUR Restaurant, tucked into a corner of the Mueang Mai Market in Sateng Subdistrict, is the answer that people in Yala pass on by word of mouth. Walk through the entrance of the Mueang Mai fresh market and glance left — the fragrance of spice from a large pot of Khao Mok will greet you before you even see the sign. This isn't just an ordinary Khao Mok stall; it's a full Arabic restaurant with over a hundred menu items covering authentic Arabic, Pakistani, Thai, and Western food, all in one place.

The star is the biryani rice: long-grain basmati cooked until every grain is beautifully separate, layered with many spices until wonderfully fragrant. For those who want firm meat, goat biryani is braised until melt-in-the-mouth tender. The chicken version comes as crispy-skin fried chicken with fragrant rice drizzled with a rich curry sauce. Beyond khao mok there's steamed sea bass with lime, garlic-stir-fried beef, punchy salads, and roti in several fillings to round off the meal. One visit covers a complete savoury-and-sweet meal without needing to move tables.

Relaxed, open market-restaurant atmosphere — clean and comfortable. Works equally well solo or as a family shared-dishes table. Very wallet-friendly — most items are well under 200 THB per person — which makes it a favourite with Yala locals and tourists looking for bold Halal food while exploring the city.

The restaurant is open nearly all day from mid-morning to evening. Anyone planning a Yala trip and looking for a Halal Arabic restaurant with full, punchy flavours in a comfortable setting should put ANNUR on the eating list. Easy to get to from central Mueang Mai Market, convenient parking, and takeaway is available for those who want to bring fragrant biryani back to their accommodation.
blocks.bestFor: Halal Arabic food with full flavour in Yala city — solo or family
blocks.hours: Open daily (Mon–Sat) approximately 10:00–21:00 (some sources list 11:00–22:00). Closed Sundays.
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: street food · Charles Haynes / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Guay Jab Na Rongrian Yala (Por Por)
blocks.signature: Old-recipe guay jab, thick-cut crispy pork, palo egg, chicken blood
blocks.descHtml:
Wake up early in Yala and want a warming bowl the way locals eat it — Guay Jab Na Rongrian Yala Bamrung Phadung Pracha (known simply as "Por Por") is the pin to drop. This long-running guay jab shop has carried its recipe down from the original grandmother for nearly 60 years. A small, neat shophouse facing the school, with a visible sign. Simply arranged tables and chairs inside, clean throughout, with the guay jab preparation station in full view as you walk in. Good for anyone wanting a straightforward early breakfast, or out-of-towners who want to try the original flavour of this city.

The star here is the thick guay jab broth: springy tube-shaped noodles, a long-simmered broth with deep, fragrant spice — nothing weak about it. The bowl comes packed: thick-cut crispy pork that fills your mouth in one bite, marinated chicken that is juicy and well-rounded, soft palo egg, and blood cubes that are clean with no gamey smell, finished with fried garlic. Reviewers who have tried it consistently say they're hooked on the rich, old-recipe flavour. Some have said they don't normally eat guay jab but finished the whole bowl here. A classic that's increasingly rare in modern times.

Price is extremely reasonable — around 35 THB per bowl, filling and honest. A breakfast that doesn't dent the wallet. The restaurant is in central Yala on Thetsaban 3 Road, Sateng Subdistrict, in the grid-planned section of the city that is easy to get to. The crucial detail: the shop opens only between around 06:00–08:00 and sells out quickly. Locals recommend arriving before 7am to get a complete bowl with all the toppings. Arrive late and you may find little left or nothing at all.

This place has remained popular not because of anything flashy, but because of the absolute consistency of the flavour it has kept alive for decades. A restaurant that Yala locals eat at out of habit, and are always happy to share with anyone from outside who asks.
mustOrder: Thick guay jab broth with assorted toppings
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: street food · Charles Haynes / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Sup Seng Yala
blocks.area: In front of Yala Railway Station, Mueang Yala District, Yala Province
blocks.signature: Sup seng / beef offal soup with fragrant spice broth
blocks.descHtml:
Come to Yala and want a meal with real local legend status? Sup Seng in front of the railway station is where Yala locals will point you first. This is one of the original beef offal soup shops in the city, beside the soup lane in front of the railway station for decades, now in its third generation. Perfect for anyone who just got off the train or is exploring the old town of Yala and wants a warming morning or late-morning bowl to start the day, or for those tracking down local food that's genuinely hard to find elsewhere.

The must-orders are sup nuea (beef soup) and sup khrueang nai (offal soup) — the restaurant's headliners. Broth slow-cooked until deeply rich, with Southern Thai spice fragrance that reviewers consistently describe as warm, rounded, and comforting. The beef and offal are tender, served with bean sprouts and spring onion. Fish sauce, dried-chilli oil, and lime are set on the table for seasoning to taste. Add a side of rice and a fried egg for a fully satisfying meal. The overall flavour is deep and full without being heavy or cloying — a Muslim-style soup you can eat comfortably through the bowl.

Simple, welcoming, old-local-market atmosphere. A big soup pot and the raw ingredients are displayed at the front in plain sight. Very friendly on the wallet — starting at around 30 THB; nothing in the restaurant goes over 100 THB. So it's a comfortable and easy-going meal. The location is easy to find right in front of Yala Railway Station. Halal-certified. Open approximately 9am to 4pm daily, closed during Ramadan.

Good to know: the mid-morning to noon window is the busiest. If you don't want to wait long, come before 10am or after 1pm. The shop closes at 4pm, so anyone who plans to eat here should aim for morning to midday. This restaurant has endured across generations because its soup flavour is consistent and its specific spice profile is unlike anything else — combined with being the go-to food landmark at Yala Railway Station for a very long time.
blocks.bestFor: Warm morning or late-morning meal right after arriving in Yala
blocks.zone: In front of Yala Railway Station

blocks.name: Kopi Slow (Kopi Slow)
blocks.signature: Traditional Kopi coffee, iced sweetened coffee, Chinese doughnut, soft-boiled egg, dim sum set
blocks.descHtml:
Kopi Slow is a traditional Chinese kopitiam café done retro-contemporary, tucked in the Old Market Soi 6 near Yala Railway Station. A place where Yala friends meet for a slow, easy morning stretching into the evening — good for anyone who wants the old-city atmosphere at a relaxed pace, a long coffee chat, or a nice photo stop while strolling through the old market. If you love old Chinese-Southern Thai food and drink, you'll be right at home here.

Almost every table orders the traditional Kopi coffee: strong, fragrant, smooth in the classic drip-bag style — and iced sweetened black coffee that hits the perfect sweet-rich balance. On the food side, standouts are Chinese doughnuts fried hot to dip in coffee, soft-boiled egg with soy sauce, and steaming bamboo baskets of dim sum that disappear easily. Some days there are also red velvet cake and pudding. Reviewers broadly agree: honest flavour, friendly price, an easy comfortable meal. Morning or afternoon snack in a single sitting.

The interior is decorated in a contemporary Chinese style that blends genuinely old elements — glazed tiles, lattice bricks, wooden furniture — making every corner photogenic. Quiet and unhurried atmosphere, good for working or sitting long. In the middle of the old market and walkable from the railway station, with some parking nearby. Open daily 10:00–22:00, good for both a mid-morning visit and an evening drop-in.

What makes this place popular among Yala locals is the combination of three things in one: familiar old-style coffee, increasingly rare old Chinese food, and a vintage photogenic setting. One small note: on holiday evenings it gets busier. For large groups, allow a bit of time to get a table. Then just settle in and take it slow, true to the restaurant's name.
blocks.bestFor: Coffee fans who love old-style drinks, relaxed morning–afternoon visit in the old town
blocks.spice: Not spicy (focus on drinks and snacks)

blocks.name: Nang Yala
blocks.signature: Roti with curry set, Khao Yum, Halal breakfast food
blocks.descHtml:
Come to Yala and want a genuine Southern Halal breakfast the way locals eat it — "Nang" (NANG Eat More Roti) on Thanawit Road is the restaurant this neighbourhood points you to. The draw is opening from 6:30am with over fifty menu items to choose from — and a fun ordering method: a tick-box order sheet where you customise your own meal. Suits the roti crowd, the rice crowd, and the hot-tea crowd equally well.

The must-order is the roti set with curry: soft roti paired with a choice of beef, chicken, or bean curry — each one a good dip. For crispiness, try the crispy roti. Real reviewers say it's "extremely crispy." For a sweet finish, roti bomb with banana — ripe banana, soft and sweet. The other must-have is Khao Yum: full of fresh herbs, clean and refreshing, a perfect contrast to the richness of the roti. The overall flavour leans slightly sweet — as typical of the Southern style. If you prefer less sweet, just let the staff know.

Simple breakfast-restaurant atmosphere, busy from early morning, lively in the way of a neighbourhood regular's place. Very light on the wallet — most people finish under 100 THB per head — making it an easy and filling start to the day. Google scores 4.5 from hundreds of reviews, reflecting that locals come back regularly.

One thing to know: the restaurant has two branches in Yala city. This Thanawit branch opens from morning to evening (Sundays close at 4pm). Holiday mornings get crowded and the queue may take a moment. For groups or early-start days, allow a little extra time. Halal-certified — comfortable for the whole family.
mustOrder: Roti set with curry (roti + beef/chicken/bean curry)
blocks.bestFor: Halal breakfast before a day of exploring Yala

blocks.title: Know Before You Eat in Yala

items.title: Getting Around
items.text: In Yala city most restaurants are close together — walkable or easy to get a ride. Grab is sparse, so rent a car or use local taxis. Betong is about 2–3 hours from the city up a mountain road. Having your own vehicle or booking a car with driver is recommended.

items.title: Carry Cash
items.text: Street-food stalls, guay jab shops, beef soup, and traditional coffee shops mostly take cash. Some larger spots have PromptPay but not all. Keep small bills on hand. Bigger seafood restaurants and Chinese restaurants sometimes accept transfers or card.

items.title: Timing Is Everything
items.text: Morning restaurants like guay jab, dim sum, and Betong chicken rice are popular from early and close before noon — arrive late and you may find things sold out or long queues. If you want the best of the morning spots, get going early.

items.title: Language and Menus
items.text: Most menus are in Thai; some Betong restaurants have Chinese-language menus too. Small shops may have no English menu — photograph the menu to translate on your phone, or jot down the names of famous dishes to show the staff. Yala people are friendly and will happily steer you toward the best items.

items.title: Halal Food Is Easy to Find
items.text: Yala has plenty of Halal restaurants — roti, Khao Yum, and Muslim breakfast food are common. Good for Muslim travellers. Guay jab and Chinese food shops often contain pork — check the sign at the entrance or ask before ordering.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: No tipping obligation at general restaurants. Street-food stalls — pay the listed price. If you're impressed by table service at a larger restaurant, a small tip or rounding up is a kind gesture, not a fixed custom.

blocks.title: Planning a Full Eating Trip Across Yala City and Betong
blocks.html:
Yala plays well when you split it into two zones. In the city, cover your breakfast stops first. Leave early to queue at Guay Jab Wing Gai Thep Wiman (Hia Tong), or Guay Jab Na Rongrian Yala (Por Por), then stop for Sup Seng in the lane in front of the railway station. Cap the morning with traditional Kopi coffee at Kopi Slow in the old market. Save the evening for Thara Seafood and its herb-grilled fish.

If you're heading to Betong, factor in the 2–3 hour mountain drive. Arrive and go straight to Tai See Hee for a morning dim sum near the tunnel. For lunch, try genuine Betong chicken rice at Sor Tor Maew. Keep the big evening meal for a Chinese banquet table at Ta Yern (Kitti) — chopped Betong chicken, steamed fish with plum, and braised pork belly with taro. Most morning restaurants close before noon, so plan the morning order carefully to avoid missing any.

blocks.text: Exploring Yala–Betong is far easier with a well-located stay. Base yourself in Yala city to walk the old-town breakfast spots and the seafood evening. Betong deserves at least one night so you can catch morning dim sum and head up to see the Aiyoeweng sea of mist. Book early on holiday weekends for the best rates.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Yala is the most famous?
faq.a: In Yala city, Guay Jab Wing Gai Thep Wiman (Hia Tong) is the most talked-about — a 70-year legend with palo-spice broth. For seafood, Thara Seafood carries the "Good Stuff of Yala City" badge. In Betong, Ta Yern (Kitti) and Tai See Hee dim sum are the two names almost every visitor seeks out.

faq.q: What are the signature things to try in Yala?
faq.a: In the city: guay jab with palo broth and thick crispy pork, herb-grilled fish, and beef soup near the railway station. In Betong: genuine Betong chicken with crispy skin — as chicken rice or chopped — old Hakka-style dishes like Khao Yok with taro and steamed fish with plum, morning dim sum, and traditional Kopi coffee.

faq.q: How much does eating in Yala cost per person?
faq.a: Morning meals like guay jab, beef soup, and traditional coffee mostly run 30–90 THB per dish. Betong chicken rice is around 60–90 THB. A light dim sum session comes in at low hundreds per head. Bigger meals like Thara Seafood or a Chinese banquet at Ta Yern (Kitti) run about 250–500 THB per person depending on how much you order.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance?
faq.a: Street-food and breakfast spots like guay jab, Sup Seng, and Kopi Slow are walk-in — just join the queue. For larger groups or holiday weekends, calling ahead for bigger sit-down restaurants like Thara Seafood and Ta Yern (Kitti) in Betong is worth it, especially on Friday–Sunday evenings.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open in the evening or late?
faq.a: Several morning restaurants in the list close before noon — Charoen Khao Man Gai Sor Tor Maew and Tai See Hee in Betong, for example. The restaurants open into the evening for dinner are on the seafood and Chinese side: Thara Seafood in Yala city and Ta Yern (Kitti) in Betong both suit evening table dining. Always check opening hours again before you go, as some places close when ingredients run out.
